subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core artifact-gated execution-progress contract for status updates and post-green follow-through, or should this remain limited to the existing run-lifecycle and stuck-session guardrails?
rationale: The request fits reliability goals but chooses new enforcement policy, persistence, timers, telemetry, and config surface that can change visible agent behavior and needs maintainer product direction before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Design
options.body: Keep this issue open and design a minimal core contract that reuses current lifecycle/diagnostic events plus SQLite-backed state for artifact-gated status and post-green follow-through.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Guardrails
options.body: Treat PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102160 and related watchdog issues as the supported path, and split only concrete remaining failures into smaller issues with live traces.

options.title: Decline Broad Enforcement
options.body: Close the direction as too policy-heavy for core and rely on existing liveness diagnostics, tool-loop detection, and operator procedures.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped Core Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and design a minimal core contract that reuses current lifecycle/diagnostic events plus SQLite-backed state for artifact-gated status and post-green follow-through.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus owns the most recent merged run-lifecycle reliability design and implementation, which is the closest current decision surface for this remaining guardrail policy.
